newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: CPO vessel Antea set to berth in Malaysia Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: CPO vessel Antea set to berth in Malaysia Nov 29.

text.p: The CPO (crude palm oil) vessel MV Antea, which has been delayed due to contamination of its tanks, will berth at Malaysia's Port Klang on Friday after leaving Indonesia on Wednesday, a port official said on Wednesay
Delays in loading the ship caused a mild supply squeeze on palm oil shipments to Europe and lifted offer prices.
European traders said one charterer had rejected the loading because the ship's allocated tanks were contaminated by a previous vegetable oil cargo.

"She (Antea) is going to berth tommorrow (November 29) at 10.00 a.m (0200 GMT) and is expected to sail out from Port Klang the following day (November 30) at 8.00 a.m. (0000 GMT) to another destination," an official at Port Klang said.
"I don't know where Antea is leaving to, but ... the ultimate destination will be Europe," he told Reuters.
The official said Antea is going to declare to discharge 4,000 tonnes of CPO to Port Klang, and then load 1,000 tonnes of CPO from the same port.
The 172-meter-long vessel arrived at Belawan, Indonesia last Sunday.
"It was carrying 3,000 tonnes of crude palm oil," a port official in Indonesia said.
It was not clear why there was a difference in the CPO loaded at Belawan and being discharged at Port KLang.
